answer: Whether an agent trades shale, sells lotus seeds, or writes a sonnet, its influence in the network’s dispute votes is proportional to collateral it locks for 30 days. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities gives the attacker no more total voting weight than keeping it in one account. To control a majority, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full lock period.
